[RLOW.5.6.5.2] Lowering `latest` adds a NOT sub-node **after the
sequence's last join**, where the anchor `d`, the first follower `m` and every
later follower are on the token ([IRET.7.10.2]). Its join test asserts no
candidate anchor that excludes the anchor with these followers
([LTHE.2.5.3]): the NOT sub-node blocks the match whenever a fact `f` of the
anchor's schema has `d.ts < f.ts < m.ts`, `m.ts − f.ts < T`, and none of the
anchor's `where` and the followers' `where`s, with `f` in the anchor's place,
answers `false` ([LNUL.4.7]).
Only the first follower's window involves the anchor ([LTHE.2.3.1]). In a
two-pattern sequence the last join is the first follower's.
